She answered him in the usual way; and, after a moment's pause, added,--

senses.gloss: give the correct answer or solution to
be sufficient; be adequate, either in quality or quantity
senses.learner: to be enough, or good enough, either in how much there is or in how good it is.
examples: A few kind words will answer; there is no need for a long letter.

senses.gloss: be satisfactory for; meet the requirements of or serve the purpose of
senses.learner: to be good enough for something, or to meet what it needs or do the job it is meant for.
examples: This small room will answer our needs for now.

senses.learner: to be the one who is responsible for something, or who must explain it and face what follows.
examples: He will have to answer for what he has done.

senses.gloss: give a defence or refutation of (a charge) or in (an argument)
senses.learner: to defend yourself against a charge or a point in an argument, or to show that it is wrong.
examples: She answered the charges against her one by one.

senses.learner: to match something, or to be in agreement with it.
examples: The man they stopped answered to the description of the thief.

senses.gloss: react to a stimulus or command
senses.learner: to act in reply to something that acts on you, or to an order you are given.
examples: The horse answered the rein at once and turned left.
It took her years to answer, even for herself, what his last words had meant.
